note: Current affairs items were checked in August 2026 - refresh them each exam cycle.

questions.prompt: Which gas is most abundant in the Earth's atmosphere?
questions.explanation: Nitrogen makes up about 78% of the atmosphere by volume; oxygen is roughly 21%.

questions.prompt: What is the chemical symbol for gold?
questions.explanation: Au, from the Latin 'aurum'. Ag is silver and Gd is gadolinium.

questions.prompt: The speed of light in a vacuum is approximately:
questions.explanation: About 299,792,458 m/s, conventionally rounded to 3 x 10^8 m/s.

questions.prompt: The SI unit of electric current is the:
questions.explanation: The ampere measures current; the volt measures potential difference and the watt measures power.

questions.prompt: At standard atmospheric pressure, water boils at:
questions.explanation: 100 degrees Celsius at sea level; the boiling point falls as altitude rises and pressure drops.

questions.prompt: Which is the hardest naturally occurring substance?
questions.explanation: Diamond sits at 10 on the Mohs scale of hardness.

questions.prompt: The pH of a neutral solution at 25 degrees C is:
questions.explanation: Below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic; pure water at 25 degrees C is exactly 7.

questions.prompt: Which vitamin is synthesised in the skin on exposure to sunlight?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet-B light converts a skin compound into vitamin D, which is needed for calcium absorption.

questions.prompt: Which organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.explanation: Mitochondria carry out respiration and produce most of the cell's ATP.

questions.prompt: Which blood group is called the universal donor?
questions.explanation: O negative red cells carry neither A/B antigens nor the Rh D antigen, so they can be given to almost anyone.

questions.prompt: Deficiency of iodine in the diet causes:
questions.explanation: Iodine is required for thyroid hormones; a shortage enlarges the thyroid gland, producing goitre.

questions.prompt: Which gas released by human activity contributes most to the greenhouse effect?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide from burning fossil fuels is the largest human-driven contributor to warming.

questions.prompt: In green plants, photosynthesis takes place mainly in the:
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts hold chlorophyll, which captures light energy to make glucose from carbon dioxide and water.

questions.prompt: The largest organ of the human body is the:
questions.explanation: The skin is the largest organ by surface area and weight; the liver is the largest internal organ.

questions.prompt: The All India Muslim League was founded in 1906 at:
questions.explanation: It was founded on 30 December 1906 at Dhaka during the All India Muhammadan Educational Conference.

questions.prompt: The Lahore Resolution was passed on:
questions.explanation: Passed at Minto Park, Lahore on 23 March 1940; the day is now observed as Pakistan Day.

questions.prompt: Quaid-e-Azam presented his Fourteen Points in:
questions.explanation: They were presented in March 1929 in response to the Nehru Report of 1928.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Governor-General of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah took oath as Governor-General on 15 August 1947.

questions.prompt: Who was the first Prime Minister of Pakistan?
questions.explanation: Nawabzada Liaquat Ali Khan, titled Quaid-e-Millat, served from 1947 until his assassination in 1951.

questions.prompt: The Objectives Resolution was passed by the Constituent Assembly in:
questions.explanation: Moved by Liaquat Ali Khan and passed in March 1949; it later became a substantive part of the Constitution.

questions.prompt: The boundary between India and Pakistan at partition was drawn by a commission headed by:
questions.explanation: Sir Cyril Radcliffe chaired the Boundary Commission; the Radcliffe Award was made public on 17 August 1947.

questions.prompt: How many constitutions has Pakistan had since independence?
questions.explanation: The constitutions of 1956, 1962 and 1973; the 1973 Constitution remains in force.

questions.prompt: The Constitution of 1973 came into force on:
questions.explanation: It was passed in April 1973 and enforced on 14 August 1973 under Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.

questions.prompt: The Parliament (Majlis-e-Shoora) of Pakistan consists of:
choices: The National Assembly and the Senate
The Senate and the Provincial Assemblies
The President and the National Assembly
questions.explanation: A bicameral legislature: the National Assembly (lower house) and the Senate (upper house).

questions.prompt: Under the Constitution, the head of state of Pakistan is the:
questions.explanation: The President is head of state; executive authority rests with the Prime Minister and the Cabinet.

questions.prompt: The 18th Amendment (2010) is best known for:
choices: Creating the office of Prime Minister
Devolving powers to the provinces and abolishing the Concurrent List
questions.explanation: It abolished the Concurrent Legislative List, strengthened provincial autonomy and trimmed presidential powers.

questions.prompt: How many general seats does the National Assembly have (after the merger of FATA)?
questions.explanation: 266 general seats, plus reserved seats for women and non-Muslims, giving a total house of 336.

questions.prompt: The total membership of the Senate of Pakistan is:
questions.explanation: The Senate has 96 members following the merger of FATA into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa in 2018 (previously 104).

questions.prompt: The highest mountain peak in Pakistan is:
questions.explanation: K2 (8,611 m) in the Karakoram is the highest in Pakistan and the second highest in the world.

questions.prompt: The longest river of Pakistan is the:
questions.explanation: The Indus runs roughly 3,180 km from Tibet through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea.

questions.prompt: The Khunjerab Pass connects Pakistan with:
questions.explanation: It carries the Karakoram Highway into China's Xinjiang region at about 4,693 m.

questions.prompt: Tarbela Dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Tarbela is on the Indus in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; Mangla Dam is on the Jhelum.

questions.prompt: The largest province of Pakistan by area is:
questions.explanation: Balochistan covers about 44% of Pakistan's land area, though it has the smallest population.

questions.prompt: The Durand Line is the border between Pakistan and:
questions.explanation: Demarcated in 1893 between British India and Afghanistan, it runs about 2,600 km.

questions.prompt: Gwadar deep-sea port is located in which province?
questions.explanation: Gwadar lies on the Balochistan coast and is the maritime terminus of CPEC.

questions.prompt: Pakistan is serving as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council for the term:
questions.explanation: Pakistan was elected in June 2024 for the 2025-26 term - its eighth term on the Council.

questions.prompt: CPEC is a flagship project of which wider initiative?
questions.explanation: The China-Pakistan Economic Corridor is the flagship corridor of China's Belt and Road Initiative, launched in 2013.

questions.prompt: Pakistan was removed from the FATF grey list in:
questions.explanation: The Financial Action Task Force removed Pakistan from its list of jurisdictions under increased monitoring in October 2022.

questions.prompt: Pakistan became a full member of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation in:
questions.explanation: Pakistan and India were both admitted as full members at the Astana summit in June 2017.

questions.prompt: The headquarters of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) is in:
questions.explanation: The OIC General Secretariat is in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. It is the second largest inter-governmental organisation after the UN.

questions.prompt: The headquarters of SAARC is located in:
questions.explanation: The SAARC Secretariat has been in Kathmandu, Nepal since 1987.

questions.prompt: Pakistan hosted the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in October 2024 in:
questions.explanation: Islamabad hosted the 23rd SCO Heads of Government meeting on 15-16 October 2024.

questions.prompt: Who has served as Secretary-General of the United Nations since 2017?
questions.explanation: Antonio Guterres of Portugal took office in January 2017; his second five-year term runs to the end of 2026.

questions.prompt: COP28 of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change was held in:
questions.explanation: Dubai, UAE hosted COP28 in late 2023, which produced the first global stocktake and a loss-and-damage fund.

questions.prompt: The International Monetary Fund is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: Both the IMF and the World Bank have their headquarters in Washington D.C.

questions.prompt: The original five BRICS members are:
choices: Brazil, Russia, India, China, South Africa
questions.explanation: BRIC was coined in 2001 for Brazil, Russia, India and China; South Africa joined in 2010, making BRICS.

questions.prompt: The Paris Agreement (2015) seeks to limit the rise in global average temperature to:
choices: Well below 2 degrees C, pursuing 1.5 degrees C
questions.explanation: Article 2 sets a ceiling well below 2 degrees C above pre-industrial levels, with efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees C.

questions.prompt: The World Trade Organization has its headquarters in:
questions.explanation: The WTO is based in Geneva, Switzerland and was established in 1995 as successor to GATT.

questions.prompt: Which country hosted the G20 Leaders' Summit in 2023?
questions.explanation: India hosted the summit in New Delhi in September 2023, where the African Union was admitted as a permanent member.

questions.prompt: The capital of Australia is:
questions.explanation: Canberra was purpose-built as the capital in a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.prompt: The largest ocean on Earth is the:
questions.explanation: The Pacific covers about a third of the Earth's surface - larger than all land area combined.

questions.prompt: The largest hot desert in the world is the:
questions.explanation: The Sahara spans roughly 9.2 million square km across North Africa.

questions.prompt: The Great Barrier Reef lies off the coast of:
questions.explanation: It stretches about 2,300 km along the coast of Queensland, Australia.

questions.prompt: Mount Everest lies on the border of Nepal and:
questions.explanation: The summit sits on the Nepal-China (Tibet) boundary at 8,849 m.

questions.prompt: The Suez Canal connects the Mediterranean Sea with the:
questions.explanation: Opened in 1869, it links the Mediterranean to the Red Sea, shortening the Europe-Asia sea route.

questions.prompt: Which country is known as the Land of the Rising Sun?
questions.explanation: Japan - the name Nippon/Nihon itself means 'origin of the sun'.

questions.prompt: The headquarters of the United Nations is in:
questions.explanation: The UN Secretariat is in New York; Geneva, Vienna and Nairobi host other major UN offices.

questions.prompt: The World Health Organization is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: The WHO, established in 1948, is based in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.prompt: Penicillin was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928 and shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for it.

questions.prompt: The theory of relativity was proposed by:
questions.explanation: Einstein published special relativity in 1905 and general relativity in 1915.

questions.prompt: The International Court of Justice sits in:
questions.explanation: The ICJ, the principal judicial organ of the UN, sits in the Peace Palace at The Hague.

questions.prompt: The Nobel Peace Prize is awarded in which city?
questions.explanation: Alone among the Nobel Prizes, the Peace Prize is awarded in Oslo, Norway; the rest are awarded in Stockholm.

questions.prompt: UNESCO stands for the United Nations Educational, ______ and Cultural Organization.
questions.explanation: United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, headquartered in Paris.
